run.question:
Look at the elasticsearch index 'app-278-events-n8c3v6q1': list which
fields it has (with their types), and using the index's actual field
names tell me how many documents in it are ERROR level.

report.summary: Index app-278-events-n8c3v6q1 exists (green, open, 27 documents, 9.7kb) and has exactly four mapped fields: app (keyword), lvl (keyword), ts (date) and txt (text) — there is no field named 'level', 'message' or '@timestamp'. The level field is therefore 'lvl'. Filtering lvl to the exact value 'ERROR' over the authorized window (ts from 2026-11-21T10:33:03Z to 2026-11-22T10:33:03Z) returns 9 documents; the same query over the tool's default one-hour window (ts 2026-11-22T09:33:03Z–10:33:03Z) also returns 9 of 27. A terms aggregation on lvl over the authorized window shows INFO 12, ERROR 9, WARN 6, totalling 27, which matches the index document count, so the entire index content was matched. The first ERROR documents (sorted by ts) are from app 'billing-278' with txt values 'payment gateway timeout 1', 'payment gateway timeout 2' and 'payment gateway timeout 3' at 2026-11-22T10:29:01Z–10:29:03Z; this is background log content and no fault analysis was requested, so no root cause is named.

The mapping of app-278-events-n8c3v6q1 has exactly four fields: app (keyword), lvl (keyword), ts (date) and txt (text). There is no field named level, message or @timestamp in this index.

A term query {term: {lvl: "ERROR"}} on app-278-events-n8c3v6q1 with time_field ts over the authorized window 2026-11-21T10:33:03Z–2026-11-22T10:33:03Z returned total 9 (relation eq), so 9 documents in the index have lvl equal to ERROR.

A lvl terms aggregation over the same window returned total 27 documents with buckets INFO 12, ERROR 9 and WARN 6 (sum_other_doc_count 0), so ERROR is 9 of the 27 documents matched and no other lvl value exists in the matched set.

The same lvl filter over the tool's default one-hour window (ts 2026-11-22T09:33:03Z–10:33:03Z) also returned total 9 ERROR documents, and the unfiltered one-hour search returned total 27 — the same counts as the full authorized window.

The three earliest ERROR documents returned (sorted by ts ascending) are _id Ey_QAqIB5zk2ychI6GnH, FC_QAqIB5zk2ychI6GnH and FS_QAqIB5zk2ychI6GnH, all with app 'billing-278', ts 2026-11-22T10:29:01Z, 10:29:02Z and 10:29:03Z, and txt 'payment gateway timeout 1', 'payment gateway timeout 2' and 'payment gateway timeout 3'.

gaps: The elasticsearch_search tool always applies a time filter on ts and refuses to run without one, so the ERROR count of 9 is scoped to the authorized window 2026-11-21T10:33:03Z–2026-11-22T10:33:03Z (equivalently the default hour for these data); any document with ts outside that window is not observable here. The windowed total of 27 equals the index docs.count of 27, which is consistent with no documents falling outside the window, but that equality is not a guarantee.
Only 3 of the 9 ERROR documents were read; the remaining 6 ERROR documents' contents are unknown.
The index mapping is read at query time, after the incident window, so it cannot prove the mapping during the window.
next_steps: If the full ERROR set of 9 documents is needed, page with from_offset or list all 9 with size 9 and source [ts, lvl, app, txt].
If ERROR volume outside the authorized window matters, that requires a different time policy or a source that can be queried without a ts filter.
